questions.question: Which foods is a good source of vitamin B12?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meats **is a good source of **vitamin B12**.
 
• This essential vitamin is primarily found in **animal-derived foods**, making meat an important dietary source for individuals following a non-vegetarian diet.
 
• Vitamin B12 plays a crucial role in various bodily functions, including the** formation of red blood cells, DNA synthesis, and nerve function.**
 
• However, for individuals following a vegetarian or vegan diet, other sources of vitamin B12, such as fortified foods or supplements, may be necessary to ensure adequate intake.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vitamin B12,** scientifically known as cobalamin, is a **water-soluble vitamin** that belongs to the group of B vitamins.
 
• It plays a crucial role in metabolism and is essential for various bodily functions.
 
• Animals require vitamin B12 as a **cofactor in DNA synthesis**, as well as in the metabolism of fatty acids and amino acids.
 
• In humans, vitamin B12 is vital for the normal functioning of the nervous system, primarily due to its involvement in the synthesis of myelin. It also contributes to the maturation of red blood cells in the bone marrow, thereby supporting the circulatory system.
 
• Unlike animals, plants do not require cobalamin for their metabolic processes and utilize enzymes that do not rely on it.
 
• Vitamin B12 is distinguished as the most chemically complex among all vitamins. Notably, for humans, it is the only vitamin that must be obtained from animal-derived foods or supplements.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about migration in India?

options.text: Migration may be rural to urban.
Migration does not depend on social factors.
Migration has pull and push factors.
It may be urban to rural areas.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Migration does not depend on social factors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Migration **does not depend on social factors is INCORRECT about migration in India.
 
• **Migration in India** refers to the movement of people from one place to another within the country's borders.
 
• This movement can be temporary or permanent and can occur due to various factors such as **economic, social, political, or environmental reasons.**
 
• Migration in India has been a significant phenomenon throughout its history and continues to shape the country's demographic, social, and economic landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• People migrate from one state to another within India for various reasons, including **employment opportunities, education, marriage, or better living conditions**. 
 
• Migration patterns in India are influenced by various factors, including economic disparities between regions, uneven development, demographic changes, social networks, government policies, and environmental factors such as droughts, floods, or natural disasters.
 
• While migration can bring opportunities for individuals and contribute to economic growth and cultural diversity, it also presents challenges, such as urban overcrowding, strain on infrastructure and services, social tensions, and exploitation of migrant workers.

questions.question: What was the capital of the Bahmani kingdom at the time of its foundation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulbarga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Bahmani kingdom, **established in** 1347 **with its capital initially at **Ahsanabad (Gulbarga)** before being moved to** Muhammadabad (Bidar) in 1425,** stood as an independent state from 1347 to 1527.
 
• Organized into four administrative provinces, known as "Taraf," the kingdom comprised *Daultabad, Bidar, Berar, and Gulbarga, *each overseen by a tarafdar or subedar.
 
• The governance of the Bahmani kingdom followed a feudal system.
 
• Encompassing the entirety of the Deccan up to the Krishna river, the Bahmani sultanate reached its zenith of influence during the tenure of Mahmud Gawan as vizier from 1466 to 1481.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gulbarga**, situated in the Indian state of Karnataka, serves as the administrative center of the Kalaburagi district and stands as the largest city in North Karnataka (Kalyana-Karnataka). 
 
• Positioned 568 km north of Bangalore, the state capital, Kalaburagi was integrated into the newly formed Mysore State (now Karnataka) under the States Reorganisation Act in 1956. 
 
• Noteworthy architectural wonders from the Bahamani Kingdom era adorn Kalaburagi, including the Jama Masjid within Kalaburagi Fort. Moreover, Kalaburagi hosts the circuit bench of the High Court of Karnataka. 
 
• In 2014, UNESCO placed several structures in the city on its "tentative list" for potential recognition as a World Heritage Site, along with others in the vicinity, under the collective name Monuments and Forts of the Deccan Sultanate.

questions.question: Who was the recipient of Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar 2017 for Kathak?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vidha Lal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vidha Lal **was the recipient of **Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar 2017 **for **Kathak**.
 
• The Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar is a yearly Indian honor presented by the Sangeet Natak Akademi to exceptional artists under 40 who have showcased their talent in music, dance, and drama. 
 
• It aims to offer national acknowledgment to artists in the initial stages of their careers. 
 
• Each year, up to 33 artists are chosen for this award, receiving a prize of ₹25,000. This award has been granted since 2006.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jitendra Maharaj **was an Indian dancer and Kathak maestro, hailing from the Varanasi Gharana. He was honored with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award by the Government of India.
 
• **Rajendra Gangani, **renowned for his inventive style and technical expertise, is an Indian Kathak dancer. He is celebrated as one of the foremost proponents of the Jaipur Gharana style of Kathak.
 
• **Geetanjali Lal,** an accomplished Indian Kathak dancer and choreographer, was bestowed with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2007.

questions.question: What is the average temperature usually in the hills of the western Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Below 25°C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **average annual temperature** hovers around **15°C (59 °F)** in the region. Frost is common in some parts, with temperatures dropping to freezing during winter.
 
• Mean temperatures vary from **20°C (68 °F)** in the south to **24°C (75 °F) **in the north. Interestingly, the coldest periods in the South Western Ghats coincide with the wettest seasons.
 
• The Western Ghats, also known as the Sahyadri mountain range, span an area of 160,000 km² along a 1,600 km stretch parallel to the western coast of the Indian peninsula.
 
• This range crosses through the states of Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the 36 biodiversity hotspots globally, it's often referred to as the Great Escarpment of India.
 
• The Western Ghats harbor a significant portion of the country's flora and fauna, with many species endemic to this region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The region is recognized as one of the** world's top ten "hottest biodiversity hotspots," **boasting a rich array of life.
 
• It hosts over 7,402 species of flowering plants, 1,814 species of non-flowering plants, 139 mammal species, 508 bird species, 227 reptile species, 179 amphibian species, 290 freshwater fish species, and 6,000 insect species.
 
• The Western Ghats are believed to be home to many undiscovered species. Notably, at least 325 globally threatened species are found in this biodiverse hotspot.

questions.question: ‘Moon Walk’ is an autobiographical work of which famous American dancer and singer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Michael Jackson**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Michael Jackson's Moonwalk"** is an autobiography penned by the American recording artist himself in **1988**.
 
• **Published by Doubleday on February 1, 1988**, shortly after the release of his "Bad" album, the book takes its name from Jackson's iconic dance move, the moonwalk.
 
• Featuring a foreword by Jacqueline Onassis, the book quickly soared to the top of the New York Times Best Seller list.
 
• Following **Jackson's passing in June 2009**, Doubleday reissued the book on October 13, 2009, in tribute to the late musician.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Michael Joseph Jackson, **an American singer, songwriter, dancer, and philanthropist, earned the title "King of Pop" for his immense impact on 20th-century culture.
 
• Renowned as one of the best-selling music artists in history, Jackson's estimated record sales exceed 400 million worldwide.
 
• With 13 Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles, he holds the distinction of being the first artist to achieve a top-ten single on the chart in five different decades.
 
• Jackson's accolades include 15 Grammy Awards, six Brit Awards, a Golden Globe Award, and an astounding 39 Guinness World Records, notably including the title of "Most Successful Entertainer of All Time."
 
• He holds memberships in prestigious institutions such as the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (twice), the Vocal Group Hall of Fame, the Songwriters Hall of Fame, the Dance Hall of Fame (where he is the sole recording artist inducted), and the Rhythm and Blues Music Hall of Fame.

questions.question: In June 2021, the Government of India extended the FAME India Scheme II that aims to give a boost to the development of Electric Vehicles until __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**March 2024**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In** June 2021, **the Government of India extended the **FAME India Scheme II** which aims to give a boost to the development of** Electric Vehicles** until **March 2024.**
 
• In March 2024, the Indian government announced the extension of the FAME India Scheme II **until March 31, 2024**, or until the allocated funds are exhausted.
 
• The scheme, which stands for Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Electric Vehicles, aims to encourage the adoption of clean mobility solutions in India.
 
• As part of this extension, an additional Rs 500 crore has been allocated to provide demand incentives for electric two-wheelers (e2W) and electric three-wheelers (e3W).
 
• This financial assistance is expected to alleviate the financial burden on electric vehicle producers and stimulate the uptake of electric vehicles across the country.
 
• The Expenditure Finance Panel has recommended an allocation of Rs. 10,000 crore for the future FAME-III initiative.
 
• Once the budget for FAME-III is sanctioned, the allocated Rs. 500 crore will be adjusted accordingly. However, the approval for FAME-III is anticipated after the upcoming elections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The extension comes as a relief for **electric vehicle (EV)** companies that were facing challenges in meeting the initial deadline.
 
• Some manufacturers, such as Ola Electric and Bounce Infinity, had to resort to significant discounts to clear their inventory by the March 31 deadline.
 
• Launched in 2019, the FAME-II plan had a three-year budget allocation of Rs 10,000 crore with the objective of promoting the adoption of electric vehicles.
 
• The targets included financing 5 lakh electric three-wheelers, 10 lakh electric two-wheelers, 55,000 electric passenger vehicles, and 7,000 electric buses.
 
• As of December 21, 2023, a total of Rs 5,422 crore has been utilized from the initiative's budget, resulting in subsidies for 12,16,380 vehicles in total.

questions.question: Which Indian Grandmaster defeated World No.1 Magnus Carlsen in the eighth round of the Airthings Masters, an online rapid chess tournament in February 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**R Praggnanandhaa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa**, an **Indian chess grandmaster (GM),** achieved a remarkable feat in **February 2022** by defeating the world's number one chess champion, **Magnus Carlsen** of Norway, in the eighth round of the Airthings Masters rapid online chess tournament.
 
• Born on August 10, 2005, in Tamil Nadu, Praggnanandhaa holds the distinction of being the fifth-youngest person to attain the title of Grandmaster (GM), following Abhimanyu Mishra, Sergey Karjakin, Gukesh D, and Javokhir Sindarov.
 
• Hailing from Chennai, he is the younger sibling of chess player Vaishali Rameshbabu, a two-time youth chess champion. 
 
• His first Grandmaster norm was earned at the World Junior Championships in Tarvisio in November 2017.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dommaraju Gukesh** is an Indian chess grandmaster who gained prominence as a chess prodigy. In March 2019, he made history by becoming the third-youngest person ever to qualify for the title of Grandmaster, as recognized by FIDE.
 
• **Nihal Sarin**, born on July 13, 2004, is another Indian chess grandmaster and prodigy. At the age of 14 in 2018, he achieved an Elo rating of 2600, making him the third youngest player in history at that time to reach this milestone.

questions.question: Which of the following states won the best tableau award at the Republic Day parade of 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2022, Uttar Pradesh **clinched the prestigious best tableau award at the **Republic Day parade, s**howcasing the theme** "One District One Product and Kashi Vishwanath Dham."**
 
• Uttar Pradesh secured second place in the people's choice category, while **Andhra Pradesh secured third place.**
 
• The results for the best tableaux and marching contingents of the Republic Day parade were announced following assessments by three panels of judges.
 
• These panels evaluated the performances of marching contingents from the three Services, Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF)/other Auxiliary forces, as well as tableaux from various States/Union Territories (UTs) and Central Ministries/Departments.
 
• Based on their assessments, the Indian Navy marching contingent emerged as the best among the three Services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Delhi Republic Day parade** stands as the largest and most significant among the parades commemorating Republic Day in India.
 
• Held annually on 26 January at Kartavya Path, New Delhi, it serves as the centrepiece of India's Republic Day celebrations, spanning three days.
 
• The parade commences from Rashtrapati Bhavan on the Kartavya Path, proceeding towards India Gate, and culminating at Red Fort.
 
• The ceremony begins with the President of India unfurling the national flag, followed by a procession featuring multiple regiments from the Army, Navy, and Air Force, accompanied by their respective bands.
 
• Additionally, tableaux representing diverse cultures from various states are showcased along the route.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Asiatic Society in 1784 in Calcutta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**William Jones**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Asiatic Society of Bengal, **established on **January 15, 1784**, by **Sir William Jones**, a British lawyer and Orientalist, aimed to promote Oriental studies.
 
• Jones inaugurated the society with the first of a series of renowned discourses. A distinguished scholar from the **University of Oxford, Jones **arrived in Calcutta (now Kolkata) on** September 25, 1783, serving as a supreme court judge**.
 
• The society was formed shortly after his arrival, receiving support and encouragement from Warren Hastings, the governor-general of Bengal from 1772 to 1785, although he declined its presidency.
 
• Based in Kolkata, the Asiatic Society owns an impressive art collection featuring works by renowned artists such as Peter Paul Rubens and Joshua Reynolds.
 
• The society's library boasts around 100,000 volumes covering various subjects, while its Sanskrit section houses over 27,000 books, manuscripts, prints, coins, and engravings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Sir William Jones**, a British philologist and orientalist, served as a puisne judge on the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal.
 
• Renowned for his scholarship on ancient India, Jones is best remembered for proposing a relationship between European and Indo-Aryan languages, later recognized as the Indo-European languages.
 
• He attained Fellowship of the Royal Society on April 30, 1772, and became a member of The Club in 1773, eventually assuming the presidency in 1780.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jonathan Duncan** served as Governor of Bombay from December 27, 1795, until his passing in 1811.
 
• **Warren Hastings, **a British colonial administrator, held various significant positions, including the first Governor of the Presidency of Fort William (Bengal) and the initial Governor-General of Bengal from 1772 to 1785.
 
• **Sir Charles Eyre**, an administrator of the British East India Company, played a pivotal role as the founder of Fort William in Calcutta and served as its President.

questions.question: Who among the following unveiled a statue of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in Pune, Maharashtra, in March 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narendra Modi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** inaugurated a towering statue of the revered **Maratha warrior, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj**, in Pune, Maharashtra.
 
• Crafted from** 1,850 kg of gunmetal, **the statue stands at an impressive height of 9.5 feet.
 
• He inaugurated a 12-kilometer segment of the 32.2-kilometer-long metro rail project, with a total investment exceeding ₹11,400 crores.
 
• The Pune Metro project is notable for being the first in India to feature aluminium body coaches, produced domestically as part of the** 'Make in India' **initiative.
 
• Prime Minister Modi laid the foundation stone for the rejuvenation and pollution abatement of the Mula-Mutha River projects in Pune.
 
• This initiative aims to revitalize a 9-kilometer stretch of the river, with an estimated cost exceeding Rs 1080 crore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Shivaji I,** an Indian ruler and a member of the **Bhonsle Maratha clan**, established his own independent kingdom by seizing territory from the declining Adilshahi Sultanate of Bijapur, laying the foundation for the Maratha Empire.
 
• In 1674, he was officially crowned the Chhatrapati of his realm at Raigad Fort.
 
• Shivaji navigated a complex landscape of alliances and conflicts with the Mughal Empire, the Sultanate of Golkonda, the Sultanate of Bijapur, and various European colonial powers.
 
• His military campaigns expanded the Maratha sphere of influence through the capture and construction of forts, as well as the establishment of a Maratha navy.

questions.question: Which is a flowerless, spore-producing plant that is usually a thin, horn - like, or needle - like capsule with spores that develops from a flat, green leaf?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hornwort**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A hornwort** is a type of plant that belongs to the division **Anthocerotophyta**.
 
• It is characterized by its flowerless nature and **ability to produce spores**.
 
• The spores are contained within a horn-like or needle-like capsule that emerges from a flat, green structure.
 
• Hornworts are non-vascular plants, meaning they lack specialized tissues for transporting water and nutrients.
 
• They are typically blue-green in color and bear a resemblance to liverworts in their gametophyte stage.
 
• However, it is the elongated sporophyte structure that gives them their name.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chara** is a type of green algae that shares similarities with land plants, featuring a complex body structure with leaf-like structures and shoots.
 
• **Celandine **is a genus of flowering plants within the poppy family, Papaveraceae.
 
• **Riccia **is a genus of liverworts characterized by their small and thalloid structure, lacking differentiation into roots, stems, and leaves.

questions.question: Papanasam Sivan was related to which of following music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carnatic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paapanaasam Raamayya Sivan, **an Indian composer and singer of Carnatic music, was honored with the prestigious** Sangeetha Kalanidhi **by **the Madras Music Academy **in 1971.
 
• Renowned as the "Tamil Thyaagaraja," Sivan's compositions, rooted in Classical South Indian music, gained popularity through the renditions of esteemed artists such as M. K. Thyagaraja Bhagavathar, D. K. Pattammal, and M. S. Subbulakshmi. Beyond his contributions to Carnatic music, Sivan also left a mark in the realm of cinema.
 
• He served as a film score composer for both Kannada and Tamil cinema during the 1930s and 1940s. In recognition of his remarkable achievements, Sivan was bestowed with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's esteemed National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama, in 1962.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Papanasam Sivan's illustrious career was adorned with numerous accolades. In 1962, he was honored with the **President's Award, **followed by the prestigious **Sangeetha Kalasikhamani Award from "The Indian Fine Arts Society, Chennai"** in 1969.
 
• His crowning achievement came in 1971 when he was conferred the esteemed Sangita Kalanidhi title.
 
• Among his notable disciples were the renowned sibling duo, D K Pattammal and D K Jayaraman, both of whom attained the esteemed Sangeeta Kalanidhi honor, further highlighting Sivan's profound influence and contribution to Carnatic music.

questions.question: As per the 2011 census, what is the sex ratio of Daman & Diu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**618**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **2011 census**, **the sex ratio in Daman and Diu **stood at** 618 females per 1,000 males**, which is notably lower than the national average of 940 females per 1,000 males.
 
• Among all the union territories, Daman and Diu had the lowest sex ratio in 2011.
 
• In contrast, Haryana exhibited the lowest sex ratio among all the states, with 877 females per 1,000 males. 
 
• As per the 2011 census data, the sex ratio in India was reported to be 943 females per 1,000 males.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Daman and Diu**, a union territory located in western India, comprises two districts: Daman and the Diu island, which are geographically separated by the Arabian Sea.
 
• The coastal town of Daman is traversed by the Daman Ganga River, from which the territory might derive its name.
 
• The term "Diu" is believed to originate from the Sanskrit word "dvipa," signifying "island."
 
• Both Daman and Diu were under Portuguese rule for over 450 years until they were integrated into the Republic of India in 1961.
 
• Daman, situated on the mainland, serves as the administrative headquarters of the union territory.
 
• In contrast, Diu is a small island located to the south of Saurashtra in Gujarat.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty for Indian citizens?

options.text: To develop philosophical temper and spirit of enquiry
To protect and improve the natural environment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To develop philosophical temper and spirit of enquiry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Constitution of India**, it is incumbent upon **every citizen to cultivate scientific temper, humanism, and the inclination** towards** inquiry and reform**.
 
• This obligation is articulated in** Article 51 A(h) of the Constitution**, introduced in 1976.
 
• The spirit of inquiry embodies a mindset of perpetual exploration, critical and creative thinking, and the forging of connections between concepts, cultures, and individuals.
 
• To foster scientific temper among students, it is beneficial to stimulate their inquisitiveness by encouraging them to pose questions and nourishing their curiosity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The fundamental duties for Indian citizens** are enshrined in **Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution, **specifically in Article 51A.
 
• These duties are as follows:
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom. To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country's composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• To develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.

questions.question: Zangtalam is the folk dance of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zangtalam **is a traditional community dance performed by the **Paite tribe of Mizoram**.
 
• This vibrant dance involves both men and women singing and dancing in unison to the** rhythmic beat of drums.**
 
• During the performance, male dancers typically form a line in front of the female dancers, who adorn themselves in colorful attire, necklaces, and earrings.
 
• The drummer serves as the leader and conductor of the dance, directing the movements of the performers.
 
• **Zangtalam **is characterized by its elegant and rhythmic steps, creating a captivating spectacle for spectators.
 
• The Paite tribe, indigenous to the region, migrated from Myanmar to Mizoram during the late 19th century.
 
• They have established communities in more than 20 villages across various districts of **Mizoram, including Saitual, Champhai, Aizawl, and Khawzawl.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mizoram**, a state located in northeast India, has **Aizawl **as its seat of government and capital city.
 
• Situated in the southernmost part of India's northeast region, Mizoram is the only landlocked state, bordered by three of the Seven Sister States: Tripura, Assam, and Manipur.
 
• It shares a 722-kilometer (449 mi) border with the neighboring countries of Bangladesh and Myanmar.
 
• Mizoram was part of Assam until 1972 when it was established as a Union Territory.
 
• In 1986, the Indian Parliament enacted the 53rd amendment of the Indian Constitution, facilitating the establishment of the State of Mizoram on 20th February 1987, marking it as India's 23rd state.

questions.question: Which of the following weight lifting styles is used in power lifting?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dead lift**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Powerlifting** is a strength sport comprising three key lifts:** the Squat, Bench press, and Deadlift.**
 
• During a powerlifting competition, **athletes aim to lift maximal weights** across these three movements.
 
• Typically, the winner is determined by the heaviest successful lift achieved in each of the three lifts and the total combined weight lifted.
 
• Powerlifters may incorporate variations of these exercises, including front squats, pause squats, and tempo squats, to enhance their training regimen.
 
• Competitors in powerlifting can opt for equipped or un-equipped lifting, the latter often referred to as "classic" or "raw" lifting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Powerlifters** engage in weight training to enhance their performance in the three competitive lifts: the squat, bench press, and deadlift.
 
• Training routines in powerlifting exhibit considerable diversity. Some methods advocate for a wide array of variations on the competition lifts, while others focus on a more restricted selection of exercises, emphasizing mastery of the competition lifts through repetition.
 
• Powerlifting features various classifications that determine rank, such as Elite, Master, and Class I, II, III, IV. Attaining the Elite standard signifies being among the top 1% of competing powerlifters.

questions.question: In 1887, whose experiment was an attempt to find the velocity of the Earth with respect to the hypothetical luminiferous ether?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Michelson and Morley**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Albert Michelson and Edward Morley** conducted the **Michelson–Morley experiment** in **1887** with the aim of measuring the **Earth's velocity relative to the luminiferous ether**.
 
• This experiment had its roots in an earlier study conducted by A.A. Michelson in Germany during 1880–81.
 
• The luminiferous ether was a theoretical concept hypothesized as the medium through which light waves propagate.
 
• In the 19th century, it was widely believed that just as water waves require a medium to travel through, light waves also required such a medium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **James Clerk Maxwell, **a Scottish physicist, formulated the classical theory of electromagnetic radiation, which unified electricity, magnetism, and light as different manifestations of the same phenomenon.
 
• **Pieter Zeeman, **a Dutch physicist, shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics with Hendrik Lorentz for discovering the Zeeman effect, which describes the splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field.
 
• **Hendrik Antoon Lorentz,** also a Dutch physicist, shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics with Pieter Zeeman for their joint discovery and theoretical explanation of the Zeeman effect, and made significant contributions to the theory of electromagnetism and the electron theory of matter.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is a tributary of the Indus river system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sutlej**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sutlej **is a** tributary** of the I**ndus river system.**
 
• The Sutlej River, also known as Satadru, is the longest of the five rivers that flow through the historic crossroads region of** Punjab in northern India and Pakistan**.
 
• It serves as the easternmost tributary of the Indus River. The Bhakra Dam, constructed on the Sutlej River, facilitates irrigation and other amenities for the states of Punjab, Rajasthan, and Haryana.
 
• Under the Indus Waters Treaty between India and Pakistan, the waters of the Sutlej River are allocated to India.
 
• These waters are primarily diverted to irrigation canals within India, such as the Sirhind Canal, Bhakra Main Line, and the Rajasthan canal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Indus River**, a transboundary river in Asia, originates in the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• It is renowned as one of the world's longest rivers, spanning approximately 3,200 km.
 
• The Indus River courses through northwestern India, the region of Kashmir, and northern Pakistan, ultimately discharging into the Arabian Sea southeast of Karachi.
 
• With a vast drainage area of about 1,165,000 square km, the Indus River basin boasts the largest expanse of perennial (multi-year) glacial ice worldwide outside of the polar regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Sone River **is a perennial river in central India, originating from Amarkantak Hill in Pendra, Chhattisgarh. It eventually merges with the Ganga River near Maner in Patna, Bihar.
 
• **The Betwa River,** stretching 590 km in length, is a tributary of the Yamuna River in central and northern India.
 
• **The Kosi River,** a transboundary river, flows through China, Nepal, and India.

questions.question: The Social Service League was founded in Bombay by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narayan Malhar Joshi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narayan Malhar Joshi **was a notable figure in India's social reform movements during the early 20th century.
 
• In 1911, he established the** Social Service League in Bombay** with the noble aim of enhancing the living standards and working conditions of the masses.
 
• The league's primary focus was on gathering and analyzing social data, engaging in discussions on social issues, and shaping public opinion on matters related to social welfare.
 
• Alongside his involvement in the Social Service League, Joshi played pivotal roles in various other organizations dedicated to social and political causes.
 
• He was a prominent member of the Servants of India Society and actively contributed to the People's Volunteer Brigade.
 
• In 1920, Joshi was instrumental in co-founding the All India Trade Union Congress, underscoring his commitment to advocating for workers' rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Narayan Malhar Joshi, **a follower of Gopal Krishna Gokhale, was a prominent Indian trade union leader.
 
• In 1920, Joshi, along with Lala Lajpat Rai, established the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC).
 
• He served as the general secretary of AITUC from 1925 to 1929 and again from 1940 to 1948.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manabendra Nath Roy, **a 20th-century Indian revolutionary, philosopher, and political theorist, founded the Mexican Communist Party and the Communist Party of India (Tashkent group).
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale, **an Indian political leader and social reformer, played a pivotal role during the Indian independence movement and served as the political mentor of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• **Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade** was a British-era Indian judge, writer, and social reformer.

questions.question: Amarsimha was one of the luminaries in the court of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amarsimha** was one of the luminaries in the court of **Chandragupta II**.
 
• Amarasimha was a renowned Sanskrit poet and grammarian who flourished in the court of Chandragupta II, commonly referred to as **Vikramaditya**, around **375 AD**.
 
• He holds a distinguished place among the nine "gems" adorning Chandragupta II's throne, collectively known as **Navratna**.
 
• Chandragupta II, the third ruler of the Gupta Empire in India, pursued the expansionist approach initiated by his father, Samudragupta, predominantly through military conquests.
 
• Historical records indicate his victories over the Western Kshatrapas, which led to the extension of the Gupta Empire from the Indus River in the west to the Bengal region in the east, and from the foothills of the Himalayas in the north to the Narmada River in the south.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kumaragupta I**, an emperor of the Gupta Empire in Ancient India, was the son of Emperor Chandragupta II and Queen Dhruvadevi. He appears to have effectively governed the territory inherited from his father, which stretched from Gujarat in the west to the Bengal region in the east.
 
• **Chandragupta I,** a monarch of the Gupta Empire, ruled over northern and central India. His title, Maharajadhiraja, suggests that he was the inaugural emperor of the dynasty.
 
• **Samudragupta, **the second emperor of the Gupta Empire in ancient India, is esteemed as one of the greatest rulers of the country's history.

questions.question: How / By whom is the Attorney General of India appointed?

options.text: Voting by the Supreme Court judges

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Attorney General (AG) of India** is appointed by **the President of India **after consultation with the Government of India.
 
• As the **highest law officer** in the country and a **member of the Union Executive**, the AG must meet the qualifications required for a Judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• Their tenure is at the pleasure of the President, allowing for removal at any time, with the Constitution not specifying procedures or grounds for removal.
 
• The AG is entitled to speak and take part in the deliberations of both Houses of Parliament, as well as joint sittings and parliamentary committees.
 
• R. Venkataramani assumed office as the 16th Attorney-General for India on October 1, 2022, succeeding K. K. Venugopal in the role.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The President of India serves as the **head of state of the Republic of India.** This position represents the symbolic head of the executive branch, holds the highest civilian status in the nation, and serves as the supreme commander of the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• Currently,* ***Droupadi Murmu **holds the office as the 15th President, assuming office on July 25, 2022.
 
• The presidency was established upon India's transition to a republic on January 26, 1950, coinciding with the enforcement of its constitution.
 
• The President is chosen indirectly through an electoral college composed of members from both houses of the Indian Parliament and the legislative bodies of the country's states and territories.
 
• These members themselves are directly elected by the citizens.

questions.question: What type of crop is rice considered in Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**subsistence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The cultivation of rice **serves different purposes in different regions of India.
 
• In **Odisha, rice** is primarily grown as a** subsistence crop,** meeting the dietary needs of the local population.
 
• Subsistence agriculture prevails among **smallholder farmers in Odisha**, where they cultivate rice primarily for their own consumption, with little surplus for commercial sale.
 
• Conversely, in Haryana and Punjab, rice is cultivated as a commercial crop. Here, agriculture has been commercialized to a greater extent, with farmers focusing on maximizing yields for profit.
 
• Rice cultivation in these regions is driven by market demand and the availability of infrastructure for commercial agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rice **holds significant importance in the Indian diet, serving as a staple food crop for a majority of the population.
 
• India ranks second in the world in terms of rice production, with cultivation occurring in diverse geographical regions such as **deltaic areas, coastal regions, and plains **in the northeastern and northern parts of the country.
 
• The cultivation of rice requires specific environmental conditions, including high rainfall (more than 100 cm annually), humidity, and temperature.
 
• It is typically grown as a Kharif crop, planted during the monsoon season and harvested in autumn.
 
• These conditions are crucial for ensuring optimal growth and yield of rice crops across different regions of India.

questions.question: The Padma Awardee 2021, Anshu Jamsenpa, has received the award for her illustrious achievements in which of the following fields?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mountaineering**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Padma Awardee 2021,** **Anshu Jamsenpa**, has received the award for her illustrious achievements in Mountaineering.
 
• **Anshu Jamsenpa**, hailing from Bomdila in Arunachal Pradesh, holds the distinction of being the first woman in the world to scale the **summit of Mount Everest twice in a single season**.
 
• She achieved this feat while also becoming the fastest double summitter, accomplishing it within a remarkable five-day period.
 
• Jamsenpa is the sole woman to achieve the fastest double ascents of the highest peak in the world.
 
• She holds the distinction of being the first Indian woman to scale Mount Everest five times and is also the first woman and mother to complete double ascents twice.
 
• Recognizing her extraordinary achievements, Jamsenpa was honoured with the Padma Shri, the fourth-highest civilian award in India, in 2021. Her remarkable journey began on May 12, 2011, when she first stood atop Mount Everest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• During the** 2013 North East India Everest Expedition**, led by **Surjit Singh Leishangthem, Anshu Jamsenpa **successfully summited Mount Everest, achieving the rare honor of standing atop the** 8,848-meter peak**.
 
• Recognizing her remarkable achievement, the Arunachal Pradesh government recommended her name for the prestigious Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award. On September 25, 2018, President Ram Nath Kovind conferred upon Jamsenpa the nation’s highest adventure award for 2017.
 
• Jamsenpa's accolades extend beyond national recognition. She was awarded the Woman Achiever of the Year 2011-12 by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FICCI) in Guwahati in June 2012.
 
• She received the CNN-IBN Young Indian Leader Award a year prior. In 2017, the Arunachal Pradesh government honoured her with the Tourism Icon of the Year Award. Furthermore, for her exceptional contributions to adventure sports, Jamsenpa was conferred with a PhD by the Arunachal University of Studies.
